newsitem.title: UK: South West Water tumbles as UK blocks bids.
newsitem.headline: South West Water tumbles as UK blocks bids.

text.p: Shares in South West Water fell sharply on Friday after the UK authorities made the surprise decision to block rival bids for the company.
Shares in South West fell 92p to 613-1/2p, shortly after the announcement.
Shares in rival bidders Severn Trent Water and Wessex Water both rallied on the news. Severn Trent climbed 33-1/2p to 609p and Wessex was up 7-/2p at 325p.
Analysts had expected the government to allow the bids against the recommendation of the MMC, which views such takeovers as against the public interest.
"I'm surprised," said Andrew Stone, analyst at Daiwa Europe. "I thought there was a strong need for price reductions in the South West region which a bid would have offered," he added.
He added that recent press comment that South West could achieve a possible dividend growth of eight percent was likely to prevent the shares from losing all of their premium related to the bids.
Marshall Whiting, analyst at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull added that though the bid premium was large, there may still be predators to come forward.
He expected Severn Trent's shares to rise as investors had anticipated tough price conditions for the group if its bid were to be allowed.
Whiting said Wessex Water's shares were unlikely to bounce as strongly, as the group had other interests besides its core water business.
South West extended its losses on a second surprise announcement that industry regulator Ofwat would seek further rebates from the group.
"That will certainly have a further negative impact on the share price, and hit revenues" Stone said "It will affect the entire sector."
